content.caseIdentity: Abhilasha v. Parkash & Ors., (2021) 13 SCC 99; 2020 INSC 546; AIR 2020 SC 4355; [2020] 11 SCR 244
content.facts: The appellant, an unmarried Hindu daughter who had attained majority, sought maintenance from her father. The Court distinguished the summary remedy under Section 125 CrPC from the substantive maintenance right under Section 20(3) of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether an unmarried Hindu daughter who has attained majority can claim maintenance from her father under Section 125 CrPC.
Whether the substantive right under Section 20(3) of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 can be enforced through Section 125 CrPC proceedings.
content.ratioDecidendi: Section 125 CrPC provides the limited summary maintenance remedy specified by that provision. An unmarried Hindu daughter who has attained majority may claim maintenance from her father under Section 20(3) HAMA, if she pleads and proves inability to maintain herself, but that substantive right must be enforced under Section 20 HAMA rather than by extending a Magistrate's jurisdiction under Section 125 CrPC.
content.holding: The appeal was dismissed, with liberty to pursue the Section 20(3) HAMA remedy. The Court held that Section 125 CrPC cannot be expanded to enforce the larger substantive maintenance right under Section 20 HAMA.
content.relevance: Leading Supreme Court authority distinguishing the summary Section 125 CrPC remedy from the substantive maintenance right under Section 20 HAMA.
